title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes, runbook patterns, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, and customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders, and SRE leadership.

Scope:
Covers incidents that affect production inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane), observability and billing pipelines that impact customer-facing SLAs, and dependent infra (GPU pools, networking, KV cache). Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks — see service runbooks for low-level commands.

Key definitions and severity matrix:
- Severity 1 (SEV1): Production outage with broad customer impact (API failing, >50% request errors, major region down).
- Severity 2 (SEV2): Significant degradation of service or partial outage (high tail latency, degradation for a subset of customers).
- Severity 3 (SEV3): Minor degradation or non-critical system issues (single tenant issue without broader impact, metric drift).
- SEV1 timeline expectations:
  1) Detect/ack: 0-5 minutes
  2) Incident declared/IC assigned: 5-10 minutes
  3) Initial public status page update: 10-15 minutes
  4) Mitigation plan active: 15-30 minutes
  5) Recovery or workaround: as soon as practical

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns triage, high-level decisions, and customer comms cadence until handed to post-incident owner. Typically senior on-call or SRE lead.
- Communications Lead: Maintains status page, PagerDuty, and customer channels updates.
- Service Owner: Deep knowledge of the impacted service; executes runbook steps and leads remediation.
- On-call Engineer(s): Responds to pages, runs commands, and validates mitigations.
- Postmortem Author: Usually the IC or Service Owner; responsible for follow-up actions.

Paging and escalation:
- PagerDuty is the primary paging tool. Escalation policy: primary -> 5 minutes -> secondary -> 10 minutes -> team lead -> 15 minutes -> director on-call.
- If PagerDuty fails, use backup phone tree (see team-specific contact list).

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection: Alert triggers or external report. Triage quickly to determine scope and severity.
2) Declaration: If criteria met, declare incident and assign IC. Document in incident channel (#incidents/<short-id>) and create incident in the incident tracker.
3) Triage & Mitigation: Run relevant service runbook, collect logs, metrics, and traces. Apply short-term mitigations to reduce customer impact.
4) Recovery: Restore service to normal operation with validated checks.
5) Communication: Keep internal and external stakeholders updated at regular intervals.
6) Post-incident: Run a blameless postmortem, create follow-up actions with owners and SLAs.

Runbook template (use for service-specific runbooks)
- Name: <service>-<alert>-runbook
- Purpose: Short description of the alert and expected impact.
- Detection signal(s): metric names, threshold values, example alerts (e.g., api_request_errors_5m > 5% AND p50_latency > 200ms)
- Quick triage checklist (first 5 minutes):
  1) Confirm alert validity (false positive check).
  2) Check deployments in last 30 minutes (CI/CD).
  3) Check region-specific metrics and infra (GPU fleet, load balancers).
  4) Identify error traces and top failing endpoints.
- Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  1) Failover to warm capacity pool (Dedicated) or alternate region routing.
  2) Disable non-essential background jobs and batch workloads.
  3) Revert recent canary if rollout correlated.
- Recovery verification: health checks, synthetic request suite, customer-facing SLO dashboards.
- Rollback and follow-up: steps to revert configuration/drivers and links to postmortem template.

Common runbook examples (short summaries)
- API high-5xx-rate:
  - Symptoms: error spike in api_gateway_5xx_rate, customers reporting failures.
  - Quick actions: rotate API instances, scale up frontend pool, roll back recent canary, enable degraded-mode cache responses.
- GPU pool degradation (high queue/backlog):
  - Symptoms: gpu_queue_length > 1000, increased tail latency, OOM alerts on worker pods.
  - Quick actions: drain and restart failing nodes, move traffic to healthy pools, increase instance counts per autoscaling policy, engage infra-runbook to inspect GPUs and kernel logs.
- KV cache corruption:
  - Symptoms: cache-miss spike with increased backend load, cache integrity check failures.
  - Quick actions: switch to read-through mode to bypass cache, restore most recent validated snapshot, run cache consistency checks.

Communication and status page templates
- Initial incident notification (10-15 minutes):
  Subject: [SEV{n}] Incident: <short-description> - Redwood Inference
  Body:
  "We are investigating reports of <short-description> affecting <scope>. Impact: <summary>. What we're doing: <initial mitigation steps>. Next update: in 15-30 minutes. Incident ID: <INC-####>."
- Periodic update (every 30 minutes until resolved):
  "Status update [INC-####]: Summary of progress, mitigations applied, customer impact, ETA if known, next update cadence."
- Resolution message:
  Subject: [Resolved] Incident: <short-description> - Redwood Inference
  Body:
  "The incident has been resolved as of <timestamp> UTC. Summary of root cause, actions taken, customer impact assessment, and remediation work items with owners and due dates. We will publish a postmortem within 3 business days."

Status page guidance:
- First public update for SEV1/SEV2 within 10-15 minutes.
- Include impacted services, regions, severity, and any known workarounds.
- Mark updates with time and author.
- When incident is resolved, update status page to "resolved" and link to follow-up postmortem when complete.

Postmortem process and template
- Timeline: Postmortem draft due within 72 hours; final published postmortem within 7 business days for SEV1/SEV2.
- Tone: Blameless, factual, timelined.
- Required sections (flat key-value friendly):
  1) Title (string)
  2) Incident ID (string)
  3) Severity (string)
  4) Time window: detected_at, declared_at, mitigated_at, resolved_at (timestamps)
  5) Summary of impact (string)
  6) Root cause analysis (string)
  7) Timeline of events (bullet list)
  8) Mitigations and recovery steps (bullet list)
  9) Action items (list of owner | task | due date)
  10) Follow-up monitoring and verification plan (string)

Sample postmortem checklist:
- Create initial incident timeline in incident tracker.
- Assign postmortem author and reviewer.
- Gather logs, traces, and relevant alerts.
- Validate root cause with service owner.
- Publish draft and assign action items with SLAs.
- Present to SRE retro within 2 weeks for SEV1/SEV2.

Game days and readiness drills
- Frequency: quarterly game days for SRE and platform teams; monthly tabletop for critical teams.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test failover routing, exercise public communications, and verify on-call escalation paths.
- Runbook for a game day session:
  1) Define failure scenario and target systems.
  2) Notify participants and observers; create game-day incident channel.
  3) Start timer and inject alerts according to scenario script.
  4) Observe triage and remediation; capture telemetry and timings.
  5) Debrief: identify gaps and create action items.

Operational metrics and SLOs (examples)
| Component | SLO | Target | Alert threshold | Owner |
| API request success rate | Availability | 99.95% monthly | < 99.9% for 15m | api-platform-team |
| Tail latency (p99) | Latency SLO | p99 < 1.2s | p99 > 1.5s for 10m | serving-runtime-team |
| Embedding throughput | Throughput | 100k reqs/min | sustained < 80k reqs/min | dedicated-ops |

On-call rotations and handoff rules
- Standard rotation: 1-week primary on-call per service; 4-week secondary rotation.
- Handover process (weekly):
  1) Primary on-call prepares a 15-minute handover doc: ongoing incidents, scheduled maintenance, escalations, outstanding action items.
  2) Optional synchronous handover meeting for active incidents.
  3) New on-call acknowledges and updates the on-call dashboard.
- Night/weekend rules: shorter escalation windows for SEV1 (3 minutes to primary) and mandatory secondary paging after 10 minutes.

Runbook governance and maintenance
- Service owners must review runbooks quarterly or after any SEV2/SEV1.
- Runbook changes follow standard change process and must include a reviewer from SRE.

Contact lists and tooling
- Primary tools: PagerDuty (paging), Slack (#incidents-<service>), Statuspage (public), Incident tracker (Jira template), Zoom/Bridge for War Room.
- Maintain an up-to-date emergency contact list in the team wiki (phone numbers and backup emails).

Appendices
- Template: Incident channel naming: #incidents-<INC-####>-<service>
- Jira incident template fields: title, incident_id, severity, started_at, resolved_at, summary, root_cause, action_items.
- Quick command snippets (examples)
  - Check API 5xx: curl -sS https://api.redwoodinference.internal/health | jq .errors
  - Restart worker pool: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<service>-workers -n prod
